title: Fabrication and Implementation of a Reference-Free Traction Force Microscopy Platform
protocol: Gather LAP from freezer and bring to room temperature.
Gather 3.4 kDa PEGDA from freezer and bring to room temperature.
Gather NVP from freezer and bring to room temperature.
Gather AlexaFluor 488 labeled PEGDA (PEG-488) from freezer and bring to room temperature.
Gather AlexaFluor 633 labeled PEGDA (PEG-633) from freezer and bring to room temperature.
Gather PEGylated RGDS peptide (PEG-RGDS) from freezer and bring to room temperature.
Measure 3 mg of LAP in an amber microcentrifuge tube.
Measure 10 mg of PEGDA in an amber microcentrifuge tube.
Measure 5 mg of PEG-488 in an amber microcentrifuge tube.
Measure 20 mg of PEG-633 in an amber microcentrifuge tube.
Measure 6 mg of RGDS peptide in an amber microcentrifuge tube.
Dissolve 3 mg LAP in 1 mL of phosphate buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4).
Use 200 μL of dissolved LAP solution to dissolve PEGDA.
Use 200 μL of PEGDA solution to dissolve PEG-RGDS.
Dissolve 5 mg PEG-488 in 80 μL PBS.
Add 2.5 μL PEG-488 solution to the pre-polymer solution.
Filter complete pre-polymer solution through a 0.2 μm polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) filter.
Place 3 μL of the pre-polymer solution on a thin flat sheet of perfluoroalkoxy alkanes (PFA).
Place flat 150 μm thick polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) strips surrounding, but not in contact with, the drop of pre-polymer solution.
Place an acrylate-silanized coverslip on the PDMS—with the pre-polymer droplet centered under the coverslip—to flatten the pre-polymer droplet to the thickness of the PDMS spacers.
Expose the sandwiched pre-polymer solution to UV light until a hydrogel is fully formed (approximately 1 min at 14 mW/cm2 of 370-400nm light).
Carefully separate the coverslip from the PDMS spacers and attach to an open-bottom Petri dish using high-performance, double-sided acrylic adhesive.
Apply pressure to the adhesive contact surface to create a complete seal between the coverslip, adhesive, and Petri dish—with care not to crack the glass.
Rinse the hydrogel in the Petri dish using sterile-filtered PBS to minimize biological and particulate contaminants.
Use image-processing or drawing software to create an image with an aspect ratio of 100:1 (e.g., 2000 pixels long x 20 pixels wide).
Create a row of 100 evenly spaced white pixels on a black background centered along the long axis of the image.
Save this image as a *.tif filetype.
Download the LSM-ROI-Generator functions available free at the software repository.
Open Matlab and find the directory of the downloaded function files.
Once in the directory, open the run_script.m Matlab script and run the script.
Select the binary *.tif file for conversion.
Then, select a folder to save regions files.
Input the desired final size, in microns, of the selected image.
Under low light conditions, add 200 μl of LAP/NVP solution to AF633.
Mix thoroughly while protecting from light.
Remove PBS solution from the Petri dish containing a PEGDA hydrogel.
Add the dissolved PEG-633 to the hydrogel to form a droplet that completely encompasses the base hydrogel.
Load the Petri dish onto the sample holder on the microscope stage and place the lid on the Petri dish.
Allow the patterning solution to soak into the hydrogel for at least 30 min in the dark.
Turn on and configure the microscope during the soak time.
Use the 488 nm laser to image the hydrogel during soaking.
Locate the hydrogel using the PEG-488 signal with appropriate filters for AlexaFluor 488.
Zero the stage position at the center of the hydrogel in the XY plane.
Find and zero the focus position on the surface of the hydrogel.
Level the hydrogel by adjusting set screws after identifying the surface position away from the XY center.
Create a separate experiment file for photopatterning within the microscope software workspace.
Set multiphoton power to 1.8% (15.5 mW at 740 nm).
Adjust scanning speed to 6 (0.1 μm/μs) and pixel size to 0.1 µm per pixel with an aspect ratio of 100:1.
Load the regions file (*.ovl) created in step 2.2 into the regions tab.
Set all regions to acquisition using a macro.
Turn on z-stack function and set spacing to 3.5 μm for a total depth of 28 μm with 9 z-slices.
Use the positions function to set specific locations on the hydrogel where the fiducial marker arrays will be photopatterned.
Ensure the z-location of these positions dictates the center position of each z-stack.
Specify additional rows and columns at each position using the tile function.
Avoid overlapping patterned regions when specifying additional rows and columns.
Make sure that patterned areas are close enough to remove empty and unusable locations between positions.
Take successive z-stack line scans of the surface of the hydrogel every 5 min as soak time approaches the 30 min mark.
Check for swelling based on changes in the location of the surface relative to the zeroed focus position during z-stack line scans.
If no change in the surface position occurs over a 5 min interval, load and run the patterning settings created previously.
Use the 488 nm laser to verify that the surface of the hydrogel did not move during patterning.
Remove the hydrogel from the microscope and aspirate the PEG-633 solution from the Petri dish.
Rinse the hydrogel 3 times with sterile-filtered PBS, making sure to completely remove rinsate between each successive rinse.
Repeat this triple rinse every 15 min for 1 h.
Allow the hydrogel to rinse in PBS overnight.
Triple rinse the hydrogel with PBS.
Quickly triple rinse the hydrogel with a 200-proof ethanol solution.
Rinse the hydrogel again with sterile-filtered PBS after ethanol rinsing.
Dissolve 20 mg of PEG-RGDS in the LAP/NVP solution prepared in step 1.
Repeat steps for patterning using the PEG-RGDS solution instead of the PEG-633 solution.
Use appropriate regions file that defines single cell patterns.
Replace PBS in the Petri dish with the cell media used for cell culture.
NOTE: Phenol red free media is recommended during image acquisition to prevent phototoxicity.
Use a widefield fluorescence microscope equipped with a structured illumination module and a high-magnification water immersion objective lens to visualize the hydrogels.
Collect a high-resolution z-stack of images spaced 0.4 μm in Z, encompassing at least 20 μm of depth from the surface of the hydrogel into the hydrogel in the patterned area.
Ensure the upper limit of the z-stack includes at least 1-2 images physically above the patterned area where only noise is present.
Prior to cell seeding, follow standard protocols for the respective cell line for cell culture and maintenance.
(Optional) Incubate the hydrogel for 24 h in media containing antibiotics followed by rinsing with normal media if sterility of the hydrogel is a concern.
Resuspend trypsinized cells in the final volume of media to be used in the hydrogel Petri dish.
Remove all solution from the hydrogel dish and replace it with cell-laden media.
Allow the hydrogel to sit undisturbed in cell-laden media for 10 min.
Move the Petri dish carefully to an incubator.
Maintain the cells in the incubator for 4 hours or until the cells are visibly adhered.
Replace the cell-laden media with cell-free media to remove unadhered cells.
Set the temperature of the incubation chamber on the microscope to 37 °C and CO2 to 5%.
Place the Petri dish on the sample holder and locate the patterned areas.
Locate a cell of interest (COI) and acquire a transmitted or fluorescent image of the COI.
Acquire a z-stack of the patterned array beneath the COI as in step 4.1.4.
Acquire a second set of transmitted or fluorescent images of the cell.
Compare the second image set to the first to determine if cell damage due to phototoxicity is observed and whether the image acquisition settings need adjustment.
Repeat steps for each cell of interest (COI).
Using data collected in step 5.2, prepare a cropped image stack around a COI.
Ensure that the bottom image of the stack shows >80% visible patterned marker columns.
Continue cropping to the uppermost image where no fiducial markers are visible above the hydrogel surface.
Include at least 20 μm of non-stressed fiducial markers surrounding the COI.
Create a cropped transmitted and/or fluorescent image matching the XY cropping of the stack.
Segment the cell by tracing its border using either transmitted or fluorescent images, whichever is more representative.
Convert the segmented image into a binary image with the interior of the cell as black (intensity = 0).
Save this binary image as Binary Mask.tif.
Collect the image stack file, transmitted image file, and binary mask file in a single folder for each COI.
Clone or download the TFM analysis functions available free at the software repository.
Open Matlab and add the directory and all subfolders of the local clone of the code repository to the path.
Set the directory within the Matlab workspace to the folder location where the prepared images in step 6.1 were stored.
Open and run the tracking.m script.
When prompted, follow the instructions to load the appropriate images, perform initial pre-processing steps, and error-check the object tracking algorithm.
Once the script has completed, open and run the dispShear.m function.
Follow any prompts during runtime to draw a line on an image representing the primary motion axis of the scanning laser during patterning.
Once the dispShear.m code has completed, run the dispSurface.m code.
Run the interpFinal3D_2.m code.
